development_calibration.purpose: distinguish libuv-worker and WorkerThread tcache arenas and derive relative candidates

exploit_logic_improvements: preserve the v24 poison source pair at ring+0x77 while carrying the fixed proof block
select the PIE record size and candidate set by exact Node binary SHA-256
cycle calibrated signed 32-bit relative-write candidates across fresh containers
derive the PIE load bias only from the held loopback leak response

reverse_engineering.rea_limitation: the installed offline ELF provider supports Linux x64 hosts, while this REA server is on Windows
reverse_engineering.fallback: readelf, file, nm, objdump and development-only GDB in WSL Ubuntu

limitations: The address leak is specific to the bundled lab application's partial-copy behavior and is not a general property of CVE-2026-111497.
The verified PIE profile is limited to the exact source-built Node 24.22.0 binary SHA-256 and Ubuntu 24.04 glibc x86-64 layout.
The calibrated heap candidate set is sensitive to application allocation order, worker lifecycle and allocator changes.
The final RCE proof used no debugger or runtime address oracle; GDB was used only in separate, proof-ineligible development calibration.
